Claims the first power saving over n^(4/3) in four decades, a landmark, by a long nonstandard contradiction argument posted 8 days ago with no human reader; the Lean scope note claims the unit-distance theorem is formalised while also saying it is 'not included', and sorry status is unknown.
events.ai_basis: The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.

why: The statement asks how many unit distances n points can determine, i.e. the value/order of u(n); nothing in the record determines it, so every substantive event is a bound. The OpenAI n^(1+δ) construction refutes Erdős's conjectured form, but that conjecture is not in the statement's wording, so it moves the lower exponent from 1+o(1) to 1+δ: bound, not whole (F4/F6). It is digested via the nine-author companion note (Gowers, Litt, Sawin et al. worked through it); that note is answered as its own row with the same AI credit from its own footnote. Sawin, Tseng and Emmerich are human bounds; forum numerics are AI-credited bounds kept as doubtful, one knocked down. Mythos is generated on secondary report only. openai-math-167 is an AI-generated upper-bound power saving, unreviewed and doubtful but not set aside. Formalisations, digests, conditional reductions, restricted classes, other norms and finite small-n enumerations are none/variant/instances. Greilhuber et al. is none rather than bound because it is weaker than the known Euclidean bound.
doubts: The OpenAI generated-vs-assisted dispute (Marcus) rests on whether a human supplied the problem only; the companion note's one-shot account supports generated. The Mythos AI role has no author quote. openai-math-167's Lean scope text is internally contradictory. Alpöge's and the #92 dates cannot be placed. Tseng says 'Generative AI made substantive contributions' but names no system and systems[] is empty, so answered none; if a model were named it would be at least assisted.
